source_text: Consideremus et tertium, quo benignitas tua in acquiescendi facilitate cernatur. Neque parentes, in quantum parentes sunt invicem licite atque legitime ad procreandos filios coniugati, Apostolus arguit [n47] . Expende quid dixeris, non argui ab Apostolo parentes, in quantum parentes sunt. Ideo ergo eos, in quantum parentes sunt, non posse diabolo fructificare, nec de his aliquid, in quantum parentes sunt, ad diabolum pertinere pronuntiat; filii autem in tantum pertinent ad parentes, in quantum parentes sunt; igitur nec rei, nec sub regno diaboli, nec arguendi a diabolo comprobantur. Ut enim hoc quod diximus, repetitione clarescat: In tantum sexuum coniunctio suboli participat, in quantum qui coniuges sunt, fiunt parentes; si autem aliquid inter se voluerint agere petulantius, vel per illicitos adulteriorum aberrare concubitus, hoc ad filios non potest attinere, qui de vi seminum, non de vitiorum obscaenitate nascuntur.
pass_a_gloss: Let us consider also the third, by which your kindness in the ease of acquiescing may be discerned. Nor does the Apostle accuse the parents, insofar as they are parents joined to one another licitly and legitimately toward procreating children. Weigh what you have said, that the parents are not accused by the Apostle, insofar as they are parents. Therefore for this reason he pronounces that they, insofar as they are parents, cannot bear fruit for the devil, nor that anything from these, insofar as they are parents, belongs to the devil; but children belong to parents insofar as they are parents; therefore they are proved neither defendants, nor under the kingdom of the devil, nor to be accused by the devil. For that this which we have said may become clear by repetition: The conjunction of the sexes shares in offspring insofar as those who are spouses become parents; but if they shall have wanted to do something more wantonly between themselves, or to wander through illicit concubituses of adulteries, this cannot attach to the children, who are born from the force of seeds, not from the obscenity of vices.

lemmas.lexica: LS semen; Blaise bodily seed vs transmitted sin

pass_b_english: Let us consider the third point, too, so that your generosity may be seen in your readiness to agree. ‘Nor does the apostle accuse the parents, insofar as they are parents, lawfully and legitimately joined to one another to produce children’ (Augustine, Marriage and Desire 2.45). Weigh what you have said: the apostle does not accuse the parents insofar as they are parents. He therefore declares that, insofar as they are parents, they cannot bear fruit for the devil, and that nothing coming from them insofar as they are parents belongs to the devil. Children, however, belong to parents precisely insofar as they are parents. Children are therefore proved neither guilty, nor under the devil’s kingdom, nor liable to accusation by the devil. To make our point clear by repetition: the union of the sexes contributes to offspring insofar as the married people become parents. If, however, they choose to behave more wantonly with one another, or stray into unlawful adulterous intercourse, that cannot concern their children, who are born from the power of seed, not from the obscenity of vices.

choices.why: Bodily seed of generation; Julian denies it carries a will's sin.
Parents insofar as parents are not guilty; keep the forensic 'in quantum parentes sunt'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
